positioning: The last five days of Christmas. Fifty more dogs. One loud finish.
story: The count stands at 28. Fifty more dogs are on their way.
Eight Bernese tumble down the stairs on Sunday. Nine Frisky Frenchies zoom through the snow on Monday. Ten Collies bring the sheep home on Tuesday. Eleven Pointers point at the Poodle on Wednesday.
On Thursday, New Year’s Eve, twelve Chihuahuas pile onto the well and the courtyard is complete. That makes 78 dogs, the exact sum of the song.
Friday is New Year’s Day. Saturday is for the dog who was not on the list.
Write down what went well this year. Write down what made you laugh. A dog would tell you the same thing. The best gifts are the ones you can sit on.
Then close the old year. The new one begins with a Saint Bernard.
rank_cap: dogs in all, by New Year’s Eve
fblocks: Tradition runs the twelve days from Christmas Day to January 5. We count to New Year’s Eve, then keep going.
Bernese, Swiss farm dogs that pulled carts. Collie, Scotland’s sheepdog. Chihuahua, named for a Mexican state.
Fireworks frighten many dogs. Keep them inside, keep the radio on and keep the door closed on New Year’s Eve.
Walk more. Chew less. Never miss a nap.
50 dogs this week. 78 in all. 50 breed weeks ahead.
days: Eight Bernese tumble down the steps in a heap. Not one of them minds.
Frenchies have bat ears and a frisky streak. Nine zoom through the snow.
Ten Collies bring the sheep home through the gate, as Collies were bred to do.
A pointer freezes to show hunters where the bird is. Eleven point at a Poodle.
The year ends with a pile of Chihuahuas on a well. Start small. Be loud.
New Year’s Day belongs to the first walk. Where will yours go?
Every list leaves someone out. The rescue dog gets the warmest bed.
last_walk:
The first dog of the year is already at the gate.
A Saint Bernard walks out of the snow, calm and in no hurry. Follow him. The new year starts with his first step.
